headline: Highest risk is TREK’s MCP/browser-enabled, allowlisted egress path interacting with mem0’s memory layer, creating medium prompt-injection and data-leakage exposure; other risks are lower but nonzero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: TREK explicitly supports MCP and browser use, so it can ingest external content and pass it through tool-use paths. mem0 is a knowledge-management/memory agent, which makes it a plausible consumer of stored or forwarded content. The pairwise bridge is not documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF TREK forwards browser or MCP content into mem0 without provenance filtering, injection is possible.
IF mem0 treats imported text as trusted memory, attacker-controlled instructions can persist.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion from browser/MCP outputs.
Add provenance tags to all imported content.
Require human review before memory writes.
Restrict MCP tools to read-only where possible.
requires-engineering: implement content-sanitization and instruction-stripping before storage.

B_data_leakage.rationale: TREK touches sensitive classes including API keys, MFA secrets, confirmation numbers, and documents, while mem0 is a memory store that may retain or surface content. TREK also has files and logs, and mem0 has no documented isolation or egress controls beyond none. Shared handling of sensitive travel data makes leakage plausible in default use.
conditions: IF TREK stores secrets or documents in memory-backed notes, mem0 may retain them.
IF mem0 exports or replays stored context into TREK outputs, sensitive data can surface.
mitigations: Exclude secrets from memory ingestion.
Redact API keys and MFA secrets before storage.
Separate logs from user content.
Limit mem0 retention for travel records.
requires-engineering: add field-level classification and access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: mem0 shows no filesystem or network write surface, while TREK has allowlisted egress and collaborative real-time sessions. The profiles do not show overlapping unrestricted write targets or shared mutable resources, so direct conflict is limited. Uncertainty remains because TREK’s MCP and files could still overlap with external integrations.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external MCP or workspace, write contention can occur.
IF TREK exposes shared mutable files to mem0, concurrent edits may race.
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces.
Disable concurrent writes to shared files.
Use per-agent credentials.
Lock shared resources during updates.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in, so it may act on upstream content. mem0’s memory role means its outputs can become persistent inputs. If TREK consumes mem0-generated facts without verification, errors can cascade into reservations, budgets, or travel plans. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF TREK uses mem0 output as authoritative planning input, mistakes can propagate.
IF downstream actions include reservations or itinerary changes, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Require verification before actions.
Show source citations for all memory-derived facts.
Block auto-booking from unverified outputs.
Add a confirmation step for itinerary changes.
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware reasoning and action gating.

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles sensitive personal data such as country visit history, email addresses, confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets, while mem0 is a memory system with no stated residency, retention, or deletion controls. That mismatch creates a plausible compliance gap around retention and subject-rights handling. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined data flow.
conditions: IF EU personal data or secrets are stored in mem0-backed memory, retention and deletion obligations apply.
IF TREK logs or exports those records without a DPA or residency controls, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Classify regulated fields before storage.
Set explicit retention limits.
Document deletion/export workflows.
Avoid storing secrets in memory.
requires-engineering: add residency and DPA controls.
